purpose: Two/four independent Sanskrit verb creations, with both all-form and per-form scores. Test whether distinct dhatus avoid nearly perfectly correlated shared-stem errors.
recipe: Each2form set contains1 intensive-causative aorist and1 intensive-causative-desiderative in Lit/Lut/AshirLin. Each4form set contains2of each. One canonical prefix per form;Parasmaipada;nonCuradi.
validity: Components use previously reviewed finite constructions and conservative rule-wide exclusions for open oracle issues. Regenerate every component and preserve all engine variants. No new morphological oracle was introduced.
selection: All192component forms are new relative to saved panels/jobs, selected before these responses. Cohorts have disjoint dhatu families within this panel.
scoring: 64unique scored tasks, not192. All rows must be correct in order. Per-form accuracy exposes how much headline difficulty comes from conjunction. These scores are not interchangeable with single-form accuracy.
limits: No guarantee of unsaturability. New procedural tasks and separate training families provide a renewable evaluation space.
Future overlapping dhatu cohorts need a dependency-aware uncertainty method; do not treat root-set hash IDs as independent linguistic families.
Two/four-form labels are provisional and do not establish benchmark thresholds before evaluation.

overall.compound_note: Each creation set or compound is one scored task. Distinct dhatu families are counted across every constituent. A root-set identifier alone does not justify a cluster-uncertainty estimate when sets overlap.

paradigm_diagnostics.metric: Headline: all specified forms correct in the versioned answer format. Secondary: individual forms correct; missing/invalid output counts wrong.
